subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In a DNA nucleotide, the three components are:
options: glycerol, phosphate and a base
ribose, phosphate and a base
deoxyribose, sulfate and a base
deoxyribose, phosphate and a base
questions.explain: A DNA nucleotide consists of a deoxyribose pentose sugar, a phosphate group and a nitrogenous base.

questions.q: How many hydrogen bonds form between guanine and cytosine in DNA?
questions.explain: Guanine and cytosine pair via three hydrogen bonds, whereas adenine and thymine pair via two.

questions.q: In contrast, increasing the concentration of a NON-COMPETITIVE inhibitor would:
options: increase the enzyme's affinity for substrate
leave Vmax unchanged
reduce Vmax because raising substrate cannot displace the inhibitor
increase Vmax
questions.explain: Because non-competitive inhibitors do not compete for the active site, additional substrate cannot reverse their effect, so Vmax is reduced.

questions.q: A transmission electron microscope (TEM) differs from a scanning electron microscope (SEM) in that the TEM:
options: can be used on living specimens
passes electrons through a thin specimen to give a high-resolution 2D image of internal structure
has lower resolution than the SEM
produces a 3D surface image
questions.explain: A TEM transmits electrons through an ultra-thin section, producing a detailed 2D image of internal ultrastructure, whereas an SEM gives a 3D surface view.

questions.q: Chloroplasts are adapted for photosynthesis by containing:
options: hydrolytic enzymes for digestion
thylakoid membranes stacked into grana bearing chlorophyll, surrounded by stroma
cristae bearing respiratory enzymes
a single circular chromosome only
questions.explain: Grana (stacks of thylakoids) hold chlorophyll for the light-dependent reactions, while the stroma is the site of the light-independent reactions.

questions.q: The resolution of an electron microscope is greater than that of a light microscope because:
options: electrons travel more slowly than light
the specimen is stained more heavily
electrons have a longer wavelength than light
electrons have a much shorter wavelength than visible light
questions.explain: Resolution depends on wavelength; the very short wavelength of an electron beam allows much finer detail to be distinguished.

questions.q: In plant cells, water potential is determined by the equation:
options: Psi = solute potential - pressure potential
Psi = solute potential + pressure potential
Psi = pressure potential - solute potential
Psi = solute potential x pressure potential
questions.explain: Water potential equals the (negative) solute potential plus the (usually positive) pressure potential exerted by the cell wall.

questions.q: A key structural difference between a prokaryotic and a eukaryotic cell is that prokaryotes:
options: lack a true nucleus and have a single circular DNA molecule in the cytoplasm
possess membrane-bound organelles and a nucleus
contain mitochondria but no ribosomes
always have a cellulose cell wall
questions.explain: Prokaryotes have no nucleus or membrane-bound organelles; their circular DNA lies free in the cytoplasm and ribosomes are smaller (70S).

questions.q: A red blood cell placed in pure water bursts (haemolysis) because:
options: solutes enter the cell by active transport
the membrane actively pumps water in
water enters down a water potential gradient and the cell has no rigid wall to resist swelling
water leaves the cell by osmosis
questions.explain: Pure water has a higher water potential than the cytoplasm, so water enters by osmosis; lacking a cell wall, the animal cell swells and lyses.

questions.q: A plant cell becomes plasmolysed when placed in a concentrated salt solution because:
options: the cell wall ruptures
water enters the cell, pushing the membrane against the wall
salt is actively pumped out of the cell
water leaves the cell by osmosis, so the protoplast shrinks away from the cell wall
questions.explain: The external solution has a lower (more negative) water potential, so water leaves the cell and the plasma membrane pulls away from the wall.

questions.q: The Golgi apparatus is mainly responsible for:
options: producing ATP
modifying, packaging and sorting proteins into vesicles for secretion
replicating DNA
synthesising ribosomal RNA
questions.explain: The Golgi modifies proteins (e.g. adding carbohydrate), packages them into vesicles and labels them for their destination.

questions.q: Many enzymes require a cofactor such as a metal ion (e.g. Zn2+ or Cl-) because the cofactor:
options: provides the activation energy directly
denatures the enzyme to expose the active site
always binds the substrate covalently
is a non-protein component needed for the enzyme to function
questions.explain: Cofactors are non-protein helpers required for catalytic activity, sometimes altering the active site shape to allow binding.
